Scrapie in mice. Agent-strain differences in the distribution and intensity of grey matter vacuolation. Five strains of scrapie agent were used as intracerebral inocula for 2 inbred mouse strains, C57BL and VM, and their F1 cross. The degree of vacuolation in specified regions of the brain, and the relative distribution of this damage in 9 regions represented as a “lesion profile”, was different for each agent. Any of the 5 scrapie agents could be distinguished from the others with a very high degree of reliability solely on the basis of these histological parameters, using either strain of mouse.
